new_symbol_range_suggestions.resistance_nonlinear_coeff: >= 0; small enough that low-|i| behavior remains near linear, but large enough that resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i) is comparable to resistance in high-current transients

derivation_notes: The fixed-resistance assumption is relaxed by taking the effective series resistance to be resistance + resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i), representing increased dissipation during larger-current portions of the discharge. This preserves passive unforced dynamics and continuously recovers the parent law when the nonlinear coefficient is zero or when |i| stays small.
change_summary: The resistor is refined from a constant-ohmic element to an amplitude-dependent dissipative element. This makes the damping in di_dt depend on current magnitude, causing stronger early ring-down damping at larger |i| than the parent fixed-resistance model can match with one shared parameter set.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The components are linear and time-invariant, specifically that resistance is a fixed constant independent of current amplitude during the release.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Current-dependent resistive dissipation, such as heating-induced increase of effective resistance during higher-current portions of the transient.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping di_dt is affine in the observed states (q,i) with one fixed damping coefficient resistance/inductance, so for a shared parameter set the decay envelope and oscillation frequency are fixed by the same constant resistance across the whole release trajectory.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same state dependence but relax fixed linear damping by letting effective resistance increase with current magnitude, so di_dt gains a state-dependent damping interaction between i and the resistive term.
response_change.observable_effect: Larger-current portions of the ring-down are damped more strongly than later small-current portions, producing amplitude-dependent envelope curvature and stronger early-cycle suppression that the parent's single constant resistance cannot match simultaneously.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the release produces currents large enough that self-heating or other current-dependent dissipation changes the effective resistance over the observed transient; negligible-current ring-down should recover the parent behavior.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories, early high-|i| segments already show stronger damping than late low-|i| segments at the same fixed component values; in holdout with larger initial energy this same amplitude-dependent damping becomes more pronounced rather than merely rescaled.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing current-dependent resistance correction, or over trajectories confined to sufficiently small |i|, the model reduces continuously to the parent linear RLC law.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Amplitude-dependent resistive damping in an unforced series RLC discharge
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Current-dependent resistive dissipation, such as heating-induced increase of effective resistance during higher-current portions of the transient.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the damping coefficient is no longer constant: it is formed by combining resistance with resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i) before multiplying by i, so the slope of di_dt with respect to i changes across the trajectory. That creates amplitude-dependent envelope curvature rather than a uniform rescaling of the parent linear decay.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The components are linear and time-invariant, specifically that resistance is a fixed constant independent of current amplitude during the release.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Effective resistance increases with current magnitude during the discharge, producing amplitude-dependent passive damping.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set resistance_nonlinear_coeff = 0, or restrict to trajectories with resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i) << resistance.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compared at fixed inductance, capacitance, and baseline resistance, trajectories reaching larger |i| show disproportionately stronger early-cycle damping and a curved decay envelope, while late low-|i| segments revert toward the parent linear ring-down. This changes the scored target mapping di_dt itself, not merely an auxiliary state, because the damping term in the i equation now depends on both i and Abs(i).
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both regimes across these conditions because its damping is linear with one constant resistance. Refitting resistance high enough to match the stronger early decay would overdamp the later small-|i| tail and shift the whole trajectory, while fitting the late tail would underpredict the initial peak suppression. The mismatch is structural: the parent lacks the amplitude-dependent interaction term resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i)*i.

evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories, early high-|i| segments already show stronger damping than late low-|i| segments at the same fixed component values; in holdout with larger initial energy this same amplitude-dependent damping becomes more pronounced rather than merely rescaled.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing current-dependent resistance correction, or over trajectories confined to sufficiently small |i|, the model reduces continuously to the parent linear RLC law.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes dissipation is strictly linear and time-invariant, omitting amplitude-dependent effective resistance during a finite-energy discharge.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The components are linear and time-invariant, specifically that resistance is a fixed constant independent of current amplitude during the release.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Current-dependent resistive dissipation, such as heating-induced increase of effective resistance during higher-current portions of the transient.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax fixed linear resistance rather than add an unrelated mechanism. In the parent, with inductance and capacitance held fixed, varying only the instantaneous state along the release gives a target mapping di_dt determined by one constant damping gain and one constant restoring gain. This creates a shortcut: one shared resistance sets the whole decay shape. In the child, the damping slope with respect to i changes with |i|, so early high-current portions of a trajectory can decay faster than later low-current portions even under the same nominal component values and no external drive. The concrete contrast is amplitude-dependent ring-down: for releases that reach appreciable current, peaks shrink disproportionately faster at the start, while small-amplitude segments approach the parent law. A single refitted parent resistance cannot reproduce both the weak late-time damping and the stronger early-time damping across such conditions, because increasing resistance enough to fit the initial decay would overdamp the later small-current segment, while fitting the tail would underdamp the initial peaks. This is admissible in passive unforced operation because the modification only increases dissipation and does not inject energy. The effect is limited if currents remain too small for resistance variation to matter; in that regime the parent may already be adequate.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.resistance: > 0; initialized near ambient_resistance and varying moderately above it during observable self-heating transients
new_symbol_range_suggestions.thermal_resistance_gain: > 0; small enough that resistance evolves over several electrical timescales, but large enough to measurably alter damping in higher-energy releases
new_symbol_range_suggestions.thermal_capacity: > 0; comparable to or larger than the electrical decay time so thermal memory is not instantaneous
new_symbol_range_suggestions.ambient_resistance: > 0; typically close to the nominal parent resistance
new_symbol_range_suggestions.heating_saturation_power: > 0; on the order of or above typical dissipative power in strong transients so saturation is observable without immediately clamping the response

derivation_notes: The fixed resistance is promoted to a thermal state that increases under Joule dissipation and relaxes toward an ambient value, with the heating drive saturating at high power to represent finite-capacity electrothermal response. The initial condition resistance = ambient_resistance represents an initially unheated resistor and does not lie on a zero-effect set once current begins to flow, so the added feedback branch is active under admissible strong ring-downs.
change_summary: The successor relaxes the fixed-environment assumption by allowing resistor self-heating to change the effective resistance during the transient. This introduces history-dependent damping and a saturating thermal response, so di_dt is no longer determined by instantaneous q and i alone.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Resistance is fixed during the ring-down except for the instantaneous current-dependent contribution resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i).
assumption_audit.mechanism: Electrothermal resistance drift: Joule dissipation heats the resistor, increasing its effective resistance on a finite thermal timescale during the free decay.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: If thermal_resistance_gain -> 0, or thermal relaxation effectively pins resistance at ambient_resistance, then resistance becomes constant and the parent law is recovered with resistance = ambient_resistance.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping di_dt depends on q and i with a fixed dissipative law -(resistance + resistance_nonlinear_coeff*Abs(i))*i, so for fixed q the damping contribution is an instantaneous function of current only.
response_change.child_relation: Release the resistor's effective resistance from a fixed parameter to a slowly evolving thermal state, so di_dt depends on q, i, and the accumulated recent current history through self-heating; for the same instantaneous i and q, the slope can differ depending on prior dissipation.
response_change.observable_effect: In larger-amplitude ring-downs the late-time decay becomes more strongly damped than early-time decay because heating accumulates, whereas the parent can only tie damping instantaneously to |i| and cannot create this history-dependent curvature change with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when Joule heating integrated over several oscillation or decay times is large enough to change effective resistance appreciably, while thermal relaxation is not so fast that resistance remains effectively instantaneous; practically, moderate-to-large initial stored energy and finite ring-down duration are required.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Across trajectories with different initial charge but fixed component values, training already contains stronger dissipation for larger-amplitude releases; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to a distinct history effect: at matched instantaneous i and q reached at different times within a transient, the child predicts different di_dt because the resistor has warmed.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: In the limit of negligible self-heating or infinitely fast thermal equilibration to a constant ambient value, the evolved resistance becomes effectively constant and the parent law is recovered.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A fixed resistance cannot encode thermal memory. To make the target mapping history dependent under the same observed q and i, the effective resistance itself must evolve as a state driven by dissipation.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: self-heating resistor with finite thermal response and saturated heating drive
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Electrothermal resistance drift: Joule dissipation heats the resistor, increasing its effective resistance on a finite thermal timescale during the free decay.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the scored mapping acquires a hidden memory coordinate through resistance dynamics, and the saturating heating term changes curvature between weak-heating and strong-heating regimes rather than merely rescaling damping.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The circuit is series-connected with fixed resistance, inductance, and capacitance.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The resistor self-heats during the transient, so its effective resistance evolves toward higher values under Joule power and relaxes toward ambient_resistance on a finite thermal timescale with saturating heating response.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: If thermal_resistance_gain -> 0, or thermal relaxation effectively holds resistance at ambient_resistance, then the successor reduces to the parent with resistance replaced by a constant ambient value.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: With fixed component parameters but different initial charge magnitudes, stronger releases show progressively increased damping later in the same ring-down; at matched instantaneous (q,i), later points on a strong transient have more negative di_dt than earlier points or weaker runs because resistance has risen thermally. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary trajectory change, because di_dt directly uses the evolved resistance state.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this across those conditions because any constant resistance chosen to fit late-time damping in strong runs would overdamp early-time and low-energy segments, while changing resistance_nonlinear_coeff still leaves damping an instantaneous function of |i| only. The child can distinguish equal q and i with different prior dissipation histories through resistance memory, which the parent's memoryless mapping cannot absorb by global refitting.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model treats resistance as fixed apart from instantaneous current dependence, omitting resistor self-heating that changes damping over the course of the transient.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The circuit is series-connected with fixed resistance, inductance, and capacitance.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Electrothermal resistance drift: Joule dissipation heats the resistor, increasing its effective resistance on a finite thermal timescale during the free decay.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-resistance assumption rather than add an unrelated new force. The parent's target mapping uses a single instantaneous damping law, so once q and i are specified, di_dt is fixed. That is a fixed-environment shortcut because the dissipative environment cannot evolve with absorbed energy. In practice, with different initial capacitor charges and all other component values held fixed, higher-energy releases dissipate more Joule power and can warm the resistor during the observed ring-down. Then the same instantaneous pair (q,i) reached later in a strong transient can produce a more negative di_dt than earlier or than in a weaker release, because the effective resistance has increased. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce this across conditions: increasing constant resistance to match late-time strong-run damping would overdamp weak runs and early-time strong-run segments, while increasing only resistance_nonlinear_coeff still leaves damping an instantaneous function of |i| and cannot distinguish equal |i| states with different thermal histories. The effect is scientifically admissible when heating is appreciable but not so extreme as to violate finite-state assumptions, and it may be weak for very small initial charge or very fast thermal relaxation.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.saturation_current_scale: > 0; comparable to the upper-middle range of transient |i| so inductance remains near linear at weak release but decreases measurably during strong releases

derivation_notes: The linear-inductor assumption is relaxed by using an incremental inductance that decreases with current magnitude, representing magnetic core saturation or nonlinear flux linkage. This changes the reactive inertia directly in the i equation without adding a new state, and the parent law is recovered when saturation_current_scale is large compared with all observed |i|.
change_summary: The successor replaces fixed inductance with a current-softening effective inductance inductance/(1 + Abs(i)/saturation_current_scale). This creates amplitude-dependent bending in di_dt beyond the parent's purely damping-based waveform changes.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The inductor is linear and time-invariant with fixed inductance over the full release amplitude range.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Current-driven magnetic saturation or nonlinear flux linkage reduces incremental inductance at larger |i| in a series RLC discharge.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Recover the parent when saturation_current_scale -> oo, or along trajectories with Abs(i) << saturation_current_scale so the effective inductance is approximately inductance.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping di_dt(q,i,resistance) uses a constant inductance, so at fixed q, i, and resistance the current acceleration scales with a single invariant denominator and only damping changes over the transient.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the fixed-inductance assumption by allowing effective inductance to decrease with current magnitude due to magnetic core saturation or flux-path nonlinearity, so di_dt gains a state-dependent denominator and the q,i to di_dt map bends with |i| even when resistance is unchanged.
response_change.observable_effect: Across releases that generate different peak |i| while holding component values fixed, the child predicts larger-magnitude early-time di_dt and a shortened high-current half-cycle at stronger releases, beyond what the parent can match with one shared parameter set that only changes damping.

evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of negligible saturation strength or over trajectories confined to sufficiently small |i| so the effective inductance is approximately constant.

evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Current-driven magnetic saturation or nonlinear flux linkage reduces incremental inductance at larger |i| in a series RLC discharge.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the denominator of the target law, introducing amplitude-dependent reactive timescale compression rather than a uniform rescaling or extra loss term. The target mapping itself changes at fixed observed q, i, and resistance, so fitting only damping parameters cannot reproduce the same timing distortion across weak and strong releases.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The inductor is linear and time-invariant with fixed inductance over the full release amplitude range.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The inductor has current-dependent incremental inductance that decreases with |i| due to magnetic saturation or nonlinear flux linkage.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Recover the parent when saturation_current_scale -> oo, or along trajectories with Abs(i) << saturation_current_scale so the effective inductance is approximately inductance.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: When comparing low- and high-release trajectories generated by different initial capacitor charge magnitudes with all component parameters shared, the child shows stronger-magnitude di_dt and visibly compressed high-current portions once Abs(i) approaches saturation_current_scale. At matched observed q, i, and resistance values, di_dt is no longer set by a single constant inductive denominator, giving curvature in the q,i to di_dt map that the parent lacks.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot absorb this across both weak and strong releases because changing resistance terms mainly alters dissipation and envelope decay, while changing inductance uniformly rescales the whole trajectory. The child instead introduces a selective high-|i| reduction of inductive inertia, so the same parameter set must produce near-parent behavior at weak current and faster reactive motion only during strong-current segments; that state-dependent timing distortion is structurally unavailable to the parent.

evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-inductance assumption, not to add another dissipative channel. Vary the release energy through the existing initial capacitor charge magnitude while holding capacitance, ambient resistance, thermal parameters, and observation protocol fixed. In the parent, higher-energy releases mainly change damping through the existing current-dependent and thermal resistance terms, so with one shared parameter set the reactive acceleration remains tied to the same inductance and the waveform timing scales too simply. In the child, once |i| enters a magnetic-saturation range, the effective inductance drops, making di_dt more sensitive to q and less inertial exactly during high-current portions. This creates a concrete target-mapping change: at the same observed q, i, and resistance, the child gives a different di_dt because the denominator now depends on |i|. The resulting contrast is a stronger early-time acceleration and compressed current extrema for stronger releases, not merely a change in the auxiliary resistance trajectory. This is scientifically admissible for inductors with nonlinear cores or effective flux-path saturation, and it is observable when currents are high enough that the inductance shift is not negligible but still within bounded operation. If all observed transients stay in a weak-current regime, the effect collapses to the parent and should not be claimed.

The circuit current and capacitor charge exchange energy through the electric and magnetic storage elements while resistance removes energy. response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping di_dt(q,i,resistance) uses a constant inductance, so at fixed q, i, and resistance the current acceleration scales with a single invariant denominator and only damping changes over the transient.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the fixed-inductance assumption by allowing effective inductance to decrease with current magnitude due to magnetic core saturation or flux-path nonlinearity, so di_dt gains a state-dependent denominator and the q,i to di_dt map bends with |i| even when resistance is unchanged.
response_change.observable_effect: Across releases that generate different peak |i| while holding component values fixed, the child predicts larger-magnitude early-time di_dt and a shortened high-current half-cycle at stronger releases, beyond what the parent can match with one shared parameter set that only changes damping.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.capacitance: positive; initialize near the nominal small-signal capacitance and allow moderate transient deviations under strong release
new_symbol_range_suggestions.capacitance_relaxation_time: > 0; comparable to or somewhat longer than the early LC oscillation timescale sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance) when dielectric memory is observable
new_symbol_range_suggestions.small_signal_capacitance: > 0; equal to the parent capacitance in the small-signal recovery limit
new_symbol_range_suggestions.capacitance_field_gain: >= 0; small to order-one fractional capacitance enhancement under strong but finite charge loading
new_symbol_range_suggestions.capacitance_field_scale: > 0; charge scale comparable to upper-middle transient |q| where amplitude dependence first becomes visible

derivation_notes: The fixed-capacitance idealization is replaced by a dielectric state with finite relaxation toward a charge-dependent equilibrium capacitance, representing polarization memory and saturating field-dependent permittivity. Choosing the new state's initial condition equal to the small-signal capacitance gives a physically admissible pre-release equilibrium and does not artificially close the feedback branch, because strong initial charge immediately drives capacitance away from that value.
change_summary: Capacitance is promoted from a fixed parameter to a relaxing internal state that approaches a saturating function of |q|. This makes the restoring q contribution to di_dt history- and amplitude-dependent, changing local oscillation curvature and timescale during strong releases.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Capacitance is constant and time-invariant throughout the free discharge.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Dielectric polarization relaxation or field-dependent permittivity causes the effective capacitance to evolve during the transient, changing the restoring voltage associated with a given stored charge.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when capacitance_relaxation_time is taken arbitrarily small and capacitance_field_gain = 0, or more generally when capacitance rapidly locks to small_signal_capacitance so the effective capacitance is constant.

response_change.parent_relation: The current acceleration depends on q and i through a resistive drop and a current-saturated inductance, with capacitance acting as a fixed linear scale so the q contribution to di_dt is always proportional to -q/capacitance.
response_change.child_relation: Release the fixed-capacitance assumption by allowing capacitance to evolve with voltage magnitude through dielectric absorption/field-dependent permittivity, so the q-to-di_dt contribution changes with the contemporaneous charge state and creates a state-dependent interaction between q and the oscillation frequency/curvature.
response_change.observable_effect: Across free decays with different initial charge amplitudes but the same component parameter set, larger-|q| portions of the trajectory show a different local oscillation timescale and q-to-di_dt curvature than small-|q| portions; the parent can only rescale this contribution with one fixed capacitance.

evolution_contract.assumption_before: Capacitance is constant and time-invariant throughout the free discharge.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Effective capacitance relaxes toward a saturating charge-dependent dielectric state during the transient.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Take capacitance_relaxation_time -> 0 with capacitance_field_gain = 0 so capacitance = small_signal_capacitance, and identify small_signal_capacitance with the parent capacitance.

evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the ideal fixed-capacitance assumption. derivation_notes: The quasi-static capacitor terminal voltage q/capacitance is refined to a rate-sensitive effective back-voltage by making the electrical restoring coefficient depend on the current loading over the dielectric relaxation timescale. This captures dielectric absorption phenomenologically without adding a new state, and it recovers the parent when polarization relaxes much faster than the LC motion or when |i| is small.
change_summary: The capacitor restoring term in di_dt is no longer determined only by q and capacitance; its effective stiffness is reduced during fast transients through a current-dependent factor tied to capacitance_relaxation_time. This creates same-q but different-di_dt curvature between slow and fast trajectory segments, consistent with polarization lag.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The effective capacitor is treated as quasi-static: once capacitance(t) is known, the capacitor voltage is fully determined by q/capacitance with no additional rate-dependent polarization contribution.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Dielectric absorption / polarization lag causes the capacitor's terminal voltage under rapid charge redistribution to depend on both stored charge and the instantaneous current, not only on the relaxed effective capacitance state.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: When capacitance_relaxation_time*Abs(i)/sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance) << 1, the rate-sensitive factor tends to 1 and the parent capacitor term q/capacitance is recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: The capacitor contribution to di_dt is a single-valued restoring term -q/capacitance, so after capacitance is set by |q| the electrical restoring slope depends only on q and not on the instantaneous current direction or discharge rate.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the quasi-static capacitor law with a rate-sensitive capacitive back-voltage so the restoring contribution depends jointly on q and i, producing different effective electrical stiffness on charging versus discharging portions of the transient.
response_change.observable_effect: At comparable |q|, high-|i| segments show altered di_dt curvature and shifted peak-current decay relative to low-|i| segments; the parent cannot create this same-q, different-slope contrast because its capacitor voltage depends only on q/capacitance.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model lets capacitance relax in time but still assumes the capacitor voltage entering di_dt is instantaneously given by q/capacitance, omitting nonequilibrium dielectric back-voltage during fast polarization lag.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The effective capacitor is treated as quasi-static: once capacitance(t) is known, the capacitor voltage is fully determined by q/capacitance with no additional rate-dependent polarization contribution.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Dielectric absorption / polarization lag causes the capacitor's terminal voltage under rapid charge redistribution to depend on both stored charge and the instantaneous current, not only on the relaxed effective capacitance state.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's quasi-static capacitor assumption rather than adding a wholly new physical subsystem. The parent already includes dielectric relaxation through the capacitance state, but in the scored target mapping di_dt the capacitor enters only through -q/capacitance. That means two times during the transient with the same q and capacitance must produce the same electrical restoring contribution regardless of whether the capacitor is rapidly discharging or recharging. Scientifically, this is a shortcut: when dielectric polarization relaxes on a timescale comparable to the oscillation, the terminal capacitor voltage is not determined solely by q and the slowly evolving capacitance state. Vary the release amplitude so that one set of trajectories explores larger early |i| while holding the component parameters fixed. Under admissible conditions with capacitance_relaxation_time not much shorter than sqrt(inductance*small_signal_capacitance), the child model predicts a same-q but different-di_dt contrast between fast and slow segments because polarization lag modifies the restoring voltage according to current direction and magnitude. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce this across conditions: changing capacitance-field nonlinearity reshapes dependence on q, and changing inductive or resistive terms reshapes i effects globally, but the parent lacks a direct q-i interaction in the capacitor back-voltage itself. Limitation: if dielectric relaxation is extremely fast relative to the LC motion, the effect collapses and the parent remains adequate.
